metadata.title: What explains Macau students’ achievement? An integrative perspective using a machine learning approach
metadata.venue: Journal for the Study of Education and Development / Infancia y Aprendizaje

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses the Macau 2018 PISA microdata (15-year-olds nested in schools) and restricts the analytic sample to students who took the reading assessment in Chinese (79.0%), yielding n=2,979. The authors report that sampling weights were considered when running the Random Forest model, but they do not provide the specific weight variable name or clarify whether weights were actually applied in the final predictive model. Because the paper does not document the exact weight variable (e.g., a W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT-type field) or the final weighted/unweighted estimation choice, the extraction treats student weights as not clearly applied. Missing-data handling is performed via MCMC multiple imputation (mice), and the dependent variable is constructed from PISA reading plausible values aggregated across 10 PVs.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used Macau 2018 PISA data and limited the sample to participants who used Chinese as the language of the test (79.0%); Portuguese test-language participants were removed due to very small size (n=34, 0.9%). The paper states that missing data were imputed using MCMC via the mice package and that all observations were used after imputation; no additional exclusion criteria beyond the language restriction are reported.

main_findings.dataset_used: PISA 2018 Reading (Macau; Chinese test-language subset; age 15)
main_findings.target_variable: Reading achievement (PISA plausible values aggregated across 10 PVs)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Random Forest regression — RMSE: 66.28 (initial 41-variable model), R²: 0.44; optimal top-20 model — RMSE: 66.17, R²: 0.43; predictive performance reported as RMSE and R² (accuracy rate mentioned but not numerically reported for the regression).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PISA 2018 Reading data for Macau students (restricted to the Chinese test-language subset), the study leveraged metacognition, enjoyment of reading, reading self-concept, and demographic factors such as grade repetition and grade level to predict reading achievement, finding that personal factors (especially metacognitive strategies and reading enjoyment) were the most important predictors and that the optimal Random Forest model explained about 43% of the variance (R²≈0.43) with RMSE≈66. This indicates that Macau reading improvement efforts may be most effective when prioritizing student-level, malleable learning strategies and reading motivation supports, while demographic and contextual factors play secondary roles, though causal effects cannot be inferred from cross-sectional prediction.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes Macau’s PISA 2018 reading assessment for 15-year-olds, restricting the sample to students who took the test in Chinese (n=2,979) and using the 10 PISA reading plausible values aggregated as the outcome. Missing data were handled with MCMC multiple imputation (mice), and the authors then trained a Random Forest regression model with 41 predictors, selecting the optimal subset via 10-fold cross-validation with five repeats. The best-performing model used the top 20 predictors and achieved R²≈0.43 with RMSE≈66.17, while the full 41-variable model had RMSE≈66.28 and R²≈0.44. The most influential predictors were personal factors—metacognitive strategies (e.g., assessing credibility, summarizing), reading enjoyment, and reading self-concept—followed by demographic factors such as grade repetition and grade level. The paper also reports an ancillary hierarchical linear model to corroborate explanatory effects, but the design remains cross-sectional, so predictive importance is not causal evidence.
